title: Teaching LLMs to Recommend and Defer in Underrepresented Epilepsy Care
abstract: arXiv:2606.31036v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Specialist epilepsy expertise is scarce in resource-constrained settings. Clinical decision-support systems must adapt to local prescribing practices and recognize when specialist review is needed. We study pediatric epilepsy care in Uganda, predicting anti-seizure medication regimens from longitudinal clinic notes. General-purpose language models achieve non-trivial agreement with physician prescriptions, but neurologists' review reveals Western prescribing defaults that do not account for local practices. We introduce MANANA, a non-parametric prompt-learning framework that learns local prescribing guidance from a small patient-level training set. MANANA turns prescription errors into auditable prompt memory, with single-agent and multi-agent variants, and improves over classical ML models, direct LLM prompting, and prompt-optimization baselines across two independently collected Ugandan cohorts. translated_abstract: 在资源受限的环境中，癫痫专科知识十分稀缺。临床决策支持系统必须适应当地处方实践，并能识别何时需要专科医师审查。我们研究乌干达的儿科癫痫诊疗，从纵向门诊记录中预测抗癫痫药物方案。通用语言模型与医生处方达到了可观的吻合度，但神经科医生的审查揭示了其中存在默认遵循西方处方惯例、未考虑当地实践的问题。我们提出了MANANA，一个非参数化的提示学习框架，能够从少量患者级训练集中学习本地处方指导。MANANA将处方错误转化为可审计的提示记忆，提供单智能体和多智能体两种变体，并在两个独立收集的乌干达队列中优于经典机器学习模型、直接LLM提示和提示优化基线。所学到的提示轨迹也
tldr: 提出MANANA非参数化提示学习框架，将处方错误转化为可审计的提示记忆，使大语言模型能从少量本地患者数据中学习乌干达儿科癫痫的本地化抗癫痫药物处方方案，并在需要时转诊至专科医师。
en_tdlr: MANANA, a non-parametric prompt-learning framework, turns prescription errors into auditable prompt memory, enabling LLMs to learn local anti-seizure medication prescribing from small patient-level datasets in Ugandan pediatric epilepsy care and defer to specialists when needed.
